title: GIS and Remote Sensing
description: Teaches students to acquire, manage, analyze, validate, and communicate spatial information—combining GIScience foundations, coordinate systems, geodatabases, cartography, spatial analysis, GPS field data, satellite and drone remote sensing, image classification, cloud geospatial computing, web GIS, uncertainty, ethics, and environmental decision support.

topics.title: Geospatial Thinking, GIScience Foundations, and Environmental Applications
topics.description: Students learn how location, scale, spatial relationships, and environmental processes become analyzable geospatial questions.

children.title: Spatial questions
children.description: The point is to translate environmental problems into questions about location, pattern, process, and scale.

children.title: Where, why there, and why it matters
GIScience concepts
children.description: Students learn the ideas behind GIS tools so they can reason beyond button-clicking.

children.title: Environmental applications
children.description: Examples show how GIS supports land, water, climate, hazard, conservation, and justice decisions.

topics.title: Coordinate Systems, Datums, Projections, and Geodesy
topics.description: This module builds the positional reference systems needed for accurate mapping and analysis.

children.title: Coordinate reference systems
children.description: Correct coordinates are the foundation of every trustworthy map and spatial analysis.

children.title: Datums and geodesy
children.description: Students learn why the Earth model matters for accurate positioning.

children.title: Projection choice
children.description: Projection decisions preserve some properties while distorting others.

topics.title: Spatial Data Models, Geodatabases, Metadata, and Data Management
topics.description: Students learn how vector, raster, tabular, and temporal data are structured, documented, and governed.

children.title: Vector and raster models
children.description: Different data models represent different kinds of spatial reality.

children.title: Geodatabases and formats
children.description: Students learn to store, query, and manage data in professional workflows.

children.title: Metadata and data governance
children.description: Good metadata makes data reusable, auditable, and ethically traceable.

topics.title: Cartographic Design, Thematic Mapping, and Geospatial Communication
topics.description: This topic develops map design as a disciplined form of visual reasoning and public communication.

children.title: Map design principles
children.description: A map should guide attention and reduce cognitive friction.

children.title: Thematic mapping
children.description: Students learn to choose classification and symbol methods that fit the data and message.

children.title: Communication and storytelling
children.description: Maps become useful when they support a clear claim for a defined audience.

topics.title: Core GIS Operations, Geoprocessing, Overlay, and Terrain Analysis
topics.description: Students practice the GIS operations used to transform spatial data into environmental insight.

children.title: Geoprocessing operations
children.description: Students learn the basic spatial transformations behind most GIS workflows.

children.title: Overlay and suitability analysis
children.description: Overlay methods combine evidence layers to support decisions.

children.title: Terrain and hydrologic analysis
children.description: Elevation data reveal slope, aspect, drainage, and landform processes.

topics.title: Spatial Statistics, Geostatistics, and Uncertainty
topics.description: This module teaches students to quantify spatial pattern, autocorrelation, interpolation, and error.

children.title: Spatial pattern analysis
children.description: Spatial statistics help distinguish pattern from randomness.

children.title: Interpolation and geostatistics
children.description: Students learn to estimate surfaces from sampled points while tracking uncertainty.

children.title: Uncertainty and error
children.description: Every geospatial product carries positional, attribute, temporal, and model uncertainty.

topics.title: GPS, Field Data Collection, Mobile GIS, and Ground Truth
topics.description: Students connect office analysis to field measurement through positioning, sampling, and validation.

children.title: GNSS fundamentals
children.description: Students learn how satellite positioning works and why accuracy varies.

children.title: Field sampling design
children.description: Field data collection must match the analysis question and validation needs.

children.title: Mobile GIS workflows
children.description: Modern GIS includes mobile collection, quality checks, and sync to central databases.

topics.title: Remote Sensing Physics, Platforms, Sensors, and Data Products
topics.description: This topic explains how electromagnetic energy, sensors, satellites, drones, and products generate environmental imagery.

children.title: Electromagnetic foundations
children.description: Remote sensing measures energy interactions with surfaces and atmosphere.

children.title: Platforms and sensors
children.description: Sensor choice controls what can be observed and at what scale.

children.title: Data products
children.description: Students learn what imagery levels and products mean before analysis begins.

children.title: Spatial, spectral, radiometric, and temporal resolution

topics.title: Image Preprocessing, Spectral Indices, and Raster Analysis
topics.description: Students learn to prepare imagery and extract meaningful spectral, spatial, and temporal information.

children.title: Preprocessing
children.description: Preprocessing removes artifacts so image values represent the environment more faithfully.

children.title: Spectral indices
children.description: Indices convert bands into interpretable indicators of vegetation, water, burn severity, and built surfaces.

children.title: Raster analysis
children.description: Raster operations support environmental modeling at pixel and landscape scales.

topics.title: Image Classification, Machine Learning, and Accuracy Assessment
topics.description: This module develops supervised and unsupervised mapping, model evaluation, and defensible classification products.

children.title: Classification approaches
children.description: Students learn to turn imagery into thematic land-cover or condition maps.

children.title: Machine learning
children.description: Modern classification uses models that require careful training and validation.

children.title: Accuracy assessment
children.description: Classification maps are incomplete without defensible accuracy reporting.

topics.title: Change Detection, Time Series, and Environmental Monitoring
topics.description: Students learn to detect land, water, vegetation, disturbance, and climate-related change through time.

children.title: Change detection methods
children.description: Students learn to measure difference while separating real change from noise.

children.title: Time series analysis
children.description: Dense image archives allow monitoring of seasonality, trends, and disturbance.

children.title: Monitoring applications
children.description: Remote sensing supports repeated environmental assessment at scale.

topics.title: Cloud Geospatial Computing, Automation, and Reproducible Workflows
topics.description: This topic brings GIS into modern scripted, cloud-based, versioned, and scalable analysis environments.

children.title: Cloud platforms
children.description: Cloud geospatial tools allow students to analyze large archives without local data bottlenecks.

children.title: Automation and scripting
children.description: Scripts make workflows repeatable, scalable, and auditable.

children.title: Reproducibility
children.description: Professional geospatial work should be documented enough to rerun and review.

topics.title: Web GIS, Dashboards, Story Maps, and Decision Support
topics.description: Students learn to publish maps and spatial analytics for stakeholders, agencies, and public audiences.

children.title: Web mapping
children.description: Web GIS turns analysis into interactive tools for broader audiences.

children.title: ArcGIS Online and open web maps
Dashboards and indicators
children.description: Dashboards support monitoring, operations, and public reporting.

children.title: Storytelling and decision support
children.description: Spatial communication should connect evidence to decisions.

topics.title: Ethics, Privacy, Bias, Accessibility, and Responsible Spatial Data Use
topics.description: This module treats spatial data as powerful and potentially harmful, requiring careful ethical practice.

children.title: Spatial privacy
children.description: Location data can reveal sensitive information and harm communities.

children.title: Bias and justice
children.description: Spatial datasets can encode historical inequities and uneven data quality.

children.title: Accessibility and responsible communication
children.description: Maps should be usable, truthful, and honest about limitations.

topics.title: Environmental Mapping Project
topics.description: The course culminates in a complete geospatial project from question and data acquisition through analysis, validation, communication, and reproducible delivery.

children.title: Project design
children.description: Students define a meaningful geospatial question and select data that can answer it.

children.title: Analysis and validation
children.description: The project combines GIS and remote sensing methods with accuracy and uncertainty checks.

children.title: Deliverables
children.description: A world-class project produces reusable analysis and clear communication.
